visual: Low-growing, vigorous creeping perennial forming a dense carpet of trailing stems clothed in rounded golden-yellow to lime-green leaves. Small bright yellow cup-shaped flowers appear along the stems in summer.
water: Keep reliably moist. Particularly well suited to damp ground and will tolerate very wet conditions.
soil: Moist, humus-rich soil; adaptable to clay, loam or sandy soils and tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Can spread vigorously by rooting stems and may overwhelm smaller plants. Foliage becomes greener in deeper shade.
prune: Trim or cut back spreading stems whenever necessary to restrict its spread and maintain the desired area.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C.
resilience: Very hardy, vigorous and tolerant of damp conditions. Establishes rapidly where moisture is reliable.
uses: Ground cover, pond margins, bog gardens, banks, slopes, path edges, rock gardens and trailing from containers.
foliage: Semi-evergreen to evergreen in mild conditions; rounded leaves emerge and mature golden-yellow to lime-green, becoming greener in shade.
container: Excellent trailing plant for containers and hanging baskets, particularly where the compost can be kept consistently moist.
